title: Tarka Dal Tadka
subtitle: Red lentils finished with a hot spiced butter pour
excerpt: Split red lentils cooked until silky, then topped with a sizzling pour of ghee, cumin, garlic, and whole chilli. The tadka is made at the last moment and poured straight over the dal.
sourceNotes: Tarka (or tadka) dal is eaten across the Indian subcontinent. This version uses red lentils and a classic North Indian tempering.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the dal base without the tadka for up to 2 months. Make a fresh tadka when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the dal base easily. Make tadka in batches per serving for best flavour.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The dal base keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Make the tadka fresh just before serving.

content.text: Tarka dal is red lentils with a spiced hot-oil pour at the end. The dal base cooks quickly. The tadka takes under 2 minutes and must go on at the last second.
Heat the oil in the medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 1 minute. Add the turmeric and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, breaking them up, until the mixture is thick and the oil starts to separate.
Add the rinsed lentils, water, and salt. Bring to the boil. Reduce to a low simmer. Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the lentils are fully soft and the dal is thick.
Taste and adjust salt. Add a splash of water if the dal is thicker than you want. Keep the dal hot on a very low heat.
Make the tadka: heat the ghee in the small frying pan over a high heat until shimmering. Add the cumin and mustard seeds. They will pop within 20 seconds.

Add the sliced garlic and dried chillies. Add the asafoetida and curry leaves if using. The garlic will colour in 30 seconds. Add the chilli powder, stir once, and immediately pour the entire tadka over the hot dal. Cover for 1 minute, then serve with fresh coriander.

items.symptom: The tadka garlic burned before the pour.
items.cause: The heat was too high or the pan was too hot before the garlic went in.
items.fix: Use medium-high rather than high heat and move quickly. The garlic should be golden, not dark brown.

items.cause: The lentils were not stirred often enough during cooking.
items.fix: Stir vigorously with a wooden spoon, adding a little hot water, until the texture smooths out.

items.cause: Red lentils need generous salt and an assertive tadka.
items.fix: Adjust salt in the dal base first. Then make the tadka on a higher heat so the spices are more deeply toasted.
